check.population: every coordination surface, record, run declaration and shared measurement a governed tree carries
check.freshness: a verdict stands until a surface's schema, a record's writer or subject, or a run's declared scope changes
check.refusal: the coordination rules fail a surface whose records name no writer or subject, a run with no declared write scope, and an index that disagrees with the directory it indexes
check.observation: each surface's records compared against its declared schema, and each run's writes compared against its declared scope
check.evidence: none: the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it
check.authority: the declared schema and lifetime of each surface, which every record and every mechanism acting on it conforms to

records.name: Stated Invariant
records.definition: A design rule that an invariant a topology relies on is written with its property in a form that could be false, the set it ranges over, the parties it binds and the thing that would object if it stopped holding.
detected_by: an invariant with no objector, or one that names no set or no bound party
measured_by: invariants stated without an objector and not marked unheld

exemplar.before: every surface has one writer → nothing counts writers → a second writer lands and every guarantee resting on the first still reads as sound
exemplar.after: property: one writer per record → set: every record on a coordination surface → parties: every writer → objector: a check failing a record whose fence names two writers

records.name: Derived Record State
records.definition: A design rule that a record's state is a query over the edges it carries, open while its satisfying artifact is unresolved, blocked while a blocker is open and absorbed once the artifact exists, so no party writes a state.

distinctFrom.reason: Derived record state applies one owning source to a record's status, while a single source of truth covers any fact, rule or configuration value.

detected_by: a record carrying a state that its edges no longer support
measured_by: records whose written state differs from the derived one
enforced_by: the coordination closure check, which refuses a judgment closure that cites an artifact and an artifact closure that cites none

exemplar.before: a record reads status: done → its artifact was later deleted → the marker still asserts done
exemplar.after: the record cites satisfied-by: <artifact> → the artifact resolves: absorbed → the artifact is gone: open, with no field anyone has to remember to change

records.name: Declared Subject
records.definition: A rule or precondition that a record carries an allocated id and a declared subject key as two fields, so a moved surface keeps the id, a renamed subject keeps the key, and two records sharing a key are a finding.

distinctFrom.reason: A declared subject keeps a record's id and its subject as two fields that survive different renames, while stable identity requires only that one identifier last the entity's lifetime.

detected_by: a record whose id changes when its surface moves, or two records about one subject
measured_by: records sharing a subject key

exemplar.before: record id = <surface-path>-<ordinal> → the surface moves → every id changes and every edge citing one dangles
exemplar.after: id = <surface-key>-<ordinal>, allocated once → subject = <declared> → a second record declaring the same subject is reported

records.name: Write Barrier
records.definition: A mechanism that lets a planned exclusive write to a shared surface proceed only once every peer is observed parked, beside a compare-and-swap that covers every other write.
detected_by: content a peer wrote missing after an exclusive write that reported success
measured_by: exclusive writes taken without every peer observed parked

exemplar.before: a tool rewrites the board whole → a peer's record written a moment earlier is gone → every check passes
exemplar.after: planned rewrite → wait until every peer is parked → write → any other write: re-read, compare its own span, refuse with the diff on an overlap

records.name: Operand-Free Outcome Surface
records.definition: A rule or precondition that a surface carrying one jointly authored product declares that one writer per record has no operand there, and settles a collision by announcement and by each author cutting its own duplicate.
detected_by: an outcome surface with no declaration that the invariant has no operand there
measured_by: outcome surfaces missing the declaration

distinctFrom.reason: An operand-free outcome surface declares where one invariant cannot apply, while a stated invariant is the form every invariant is written in.

exemplar.before: a class statement written by several parties → the one-writer invariant is assumed to hold → nothing objects when two parties write the same clause
exemplar.after: the surface declares: one writer per record has no operand here → a collision is announced → each author cuts its own duplicate

records.name: Projection Channel
records.definition: A rule or precondition that the projection a host injects into every bounded reader is refreshed in the same change as the fact it carries, in a shape a check reads.
detected_by: a projection line that disagrees with the surface it summarizes
measured_by: changes that moved a projected fact without the projection

exemplar.before: a seat goes inactive on the board → the injected line still lists it → every spawned reader plans around a party that is gone
exemplar.after: the board write and the projection write land in one change → a check reads the projection's declared shape

records.name: Two-Direction Index
records.definition: A mechanism that generates an index from the directory on every run and checks it both ways, reporting an entry with no file and a file with no entry, with every scan independent of depth.
detected_by: an index entry that resolves to no file, or a file no entry names
measured_by: index entries and files missing their counterpart

exemplar.before: the agent index is edited by hand → a seat is added without an entry → the scan covers fewer seats than it claims
exemplar.after: the index is generated from the directory → an entry with no file fails → a file with no entry fails

records.name: Independent Lifetime Axes
records.definition: A design rule that a surface's lifetime is declared on three independent axes, retention, mutability and removal authority, each taking a value from a closed set, so no single word stands for all three.

distinctFrom.reason: Independent lifetime axes declare mutability as one of three questions about a surface, while immutability is the single rule that a value never changes after it is created.

detected_by: a surface whose lifetime names retention alone
measured_by: surfaces missing a value on any axis
enforced_by: the coordination declaration check, which reports a mechanism named for a lifetime axis that never reads that axis

exemplar.before: lifetime: deleted on close → a sweep implements it faithfully → the argument behind a ruling is destroyed
exemplar.after: retention: kept → mutability: frozen → removal authority: nobody → closing moves the surface to the archive

records.name: Section Lifetime Divergence
records.definition: A rule or precondition that a file states a default lifetime and each section declares only the axes on which it differs, since the narrower unit is the more constrained one.
detected_by: an operation permitted by the file's lifetime acting on a section whose own lifetime forbids it
measured_by: divergent sections carrying no declaration

exemplar.before: a document declares owner-rewritable → its contract block is rewritten by a sweep that the file's word allowed
exemplar.after: file default: owner-rewritable → contract block: mutability frozen → the sweep skips the block

records.name: Write Scope and Read Population
records.definition: A design rule that a run declares the paths it writes and publishes the set it read as two declarations, because collision is decided by the first and a published result's validity by the second.

distinctFrom.reason: Write scope and read population separate what a run touches from what it read, while determinism requires that the same inputs produce the same result.

detected_by: a run that reads more than it writes and publishes only its write scope
measured_by: runs publishing no read population
enforced_by: the coordination writer check, which fails a writer a run reaches outside the sanctioned set

exemplar.before: a run declares scope: <subtree> → it also reads a sibling tree → a later caller reuses its result for the sibling and gets a verdict nobody measured
exemplar.after: write scope: <subtree> → read population: <subtree> + <sibling> → the collision test reads the first, the coverage test reads the second

records.name: Read-Time Join
records.definition: A mechanism that lets a caller whose question a live declared scope already covers read that run's published result and its standing, writing nothing, so it cannot deadlock, be orphaned or need cleanup.
detected_by: two runs over one covered question, or a caller waiting on another run's handle
measured_by: duplicate runs a live scope covered

distinctFrom.reason: A read-time join is the mechanism that serves a covered question from a published result, while a joiner is the caller that uses it.

exemplar.before: a second caller starts the same measurement → both write the same report → the second waits on the first's lock
exemplar.after: caller → does a live scope cover the question? yes: read the published result and its standing, write nothing → no: start, and only then enter the collision comparison

records.name: One-Sided Liveness
records.definition: A design rule that a process's absence proves it is dead while its presence proves nothing, so liveness is derived once, from the witness first and from a generous window only where the witness cannot decide.

distinctFrom.reason: One-sided liveness decides what a process's presence can prove, while determinism requires that the same inputs produce the same result.

detected_by: two consumers of one liveness question reaching different answers
measured_by: liveness derivations outside the single one

exemplar.before: a process id is present → the claim is kept → the id was reused by an unrelated process and the claim never expires
exemplar.after: id absent: dead → id present: undecided → fall to the window, set long, because too short loses a write and too long costs one re-run

records.name: Reversible Channel Encoding
records.definition: A rule or precondition that a channel name is a total and invertible encoding of the scope it belongs to, with an alphabet that excludes the separator, so a retention check can read the scope back out of the name.

distinctFrom.reason: A reversible channel encoding lets the owning scope be read back out of a name, while stable identity requires only that the name not change.

detected_by: a channel whose name decodes to no scope
measured_by: channels no remover can attribute to a scope
enforced_by: the coordination channel check, which reports a channel whose decoded scope resolves to nothing

exemplar.before: channel = digest(<scope>) → channels never collide → no check can tell which channel is stale
exemplar.after: channel = encode(<scope>), invertible → decode(channel) resolves to nothing → the declared remover deletes it

records.name: Declare-Before-Read Order
records.definition: A mechanism that orders two simultaneous starters without a lock by writing each entry before reading the set, with the start stamp and then the party identity breaking a tie.
detected_by: two runs over one scope that both proceeded
measured_by: simultaneous starters that both proceeded

exemplar.before: starter A reads: nobody → starter B reads: nobody → both write → both proceed
exemplar.after: A writes its entry → B writes its entry → each reads both → the earlier stamp proceeds, the other exits without writing

records.name: Period-Decided Disposition
records.definition: A design rule that a duplicate is first counted by its distinguished copies and then read by the period of each derivation edge, so a periodic copy owes a comparator and a one-shot copy is a record whose source is repaired instead.

distinctFrom.reason: Period-decided disposition decides what to do with the copies a fact already has, while a single source of truth is the state it restores.

detected_by: a collapse that removed a copy written once against an earlier state of its source
measured_by: copies collapsed across one-shot edges

exemplar.before: a rule stated in code and in several documents → every document copy is rewritten to match → the record of what each surface said when it was written is gone
exemplar.after: one distinguished copy: a direction → every other edge one-shot: diagnose the copies, repair the source → a copy no party reaches: add it

records.name: Derived Party Count
records.definition: A design rule that the number of parties a body of work implies is derived from how the work is partitioned into concerns, so two parties holding one partition reach one count.

distinctFrom.reason: A derived party count ties allocation to a partition of the work, while determinism requires that the same inputs produce the same result.

detected_by: a count that moved while no partition moved
measured_by: counts proposed with no partition behind them
enforced_by: none: no mechanism derives the partition, so the count rests on review

exemplar.before: the work gets a fixed number of parties → surfaces are split to give each one something → contradictions pile up on the shared ones
exemplar.after: coupling relation → connected components → concerns → floor: concerns that must contradict each other → ceiling: the worst fan-in

records.name: Fan-In Ceiling
records.definition: A rule or precondition that the useful number of parties is bounded by the fan-in of the most contended surface, where claims resting on it go stale faster than they help.
detected_by: a surface whose claims are answered more often than they are used
measured_by: stale claims published per surface
enforced_by: none: no mechanism counts fan-in, so the bound rests on review

exemplar.before: more parties join → each composes claims about one shared surface → every stale claim is read and answered by every other party
exemplar.after: fan-in measured from recorded authorship and citations → the surface above the ceiling is split or its claims arrive marked stale

records.name: State-Arity Limit
records.definition: A rule or precondition that a property relating two states of content, such as growing but never shrinking, is enforced only by a mechanism holding both readings, in the layer that already spans runs.
detected_by: content removed from a required section while every single-state check passes
measured_by: change rules held only by single-state checks

exemplar.before: a check requires the section → it passes from empty to full and from full to empty alike
exemplar.after: the spanning layer records the section's extent per run → the next run compares → shortened: refuse → the sets differ: not comparable, refuse rather than compute

records.name: Carrier and Payload Split
records.definition: A design rule that a surface read through a tool types the fields a mechanism joins on and leaves the fields only a reader consumes as prose, deciding the line per field.

distinctFrom.reason: The carrier and payload split decides which fields are typed at all, while a closed vocabulary governs the words a typed name slot may take.

detected_by: a mechanism parsing a prose field, or a carrier and a payload that answer one question differently
measured_by: fields no declaration assigns to either side
enforced_by: none: whether a value is resolvable is a judgment at authoring, so the split rests on review

exemplar.before: a status sentence is parsed for the word done → a reader edits the sentence → the parse misreads it
exemplar.after: state: <closed value> as the carrier → reason: <prose> as the payload → the mechanism reads the key and never the sentence

records.name: Joinable Mandated Field
records.definition: A rule or precondition that a mandated field takes a value from a closed set or an identifier, or declares that it is written for readers, so a governed surface never looks measured on a property nothing can read.
detected_by: a mandated prose field that no declaration marks as written for readers
measured_by: mandated fields in neither a resolvable form nor declared for readers

exemplar.before: every record must carry a lifetime paragraph → each author writes one → nothing can join on it
exemplar.after: lifetime: retention <value>, mutability <value>, removal authority <value> → a check joins on the three values

records.name: Single Aggregate
records.definition: A rule or precondition that a shared measurement keeps one aggregate, overwritten by each run that can honestly replace it, while a run that cannot streams its verdict instead of writing a second report.
detected_by: a second report describing the aggregate's subject
measured_by: reports beside the aggregate

exemplar.before: a narrowed run writes report.<scope>.json → the directory fills with reports each true of one moment → none of them is the state
exemplar.after: a full run overwrites the aggregate → a narrowed run prints its verdict and writes nothing

records.name: Contradicted Invariant
records.definition: A defect in which one surface states the opposite of an invariant another relies on, so every mechanism faithfully implementing either statement stays green while the invariant is violated.
records.formed_by: restating an invariant in a second surface and changing only one of the copies
detected_by: two statements of one invariant that no single query ranges over
measured_by: invariants whose copies disagree

exemplar.before: the model states one writer per record → a template states one writer per file → a tool built from the template rewrites whole files and every check passes
exemplar.after: every copy of the invariant is listed → a change re-derives the set → the most delivered copy is updated first

records.name: Written Status Marker
records.definition: A defect in which a party writes a record's state as a marker instead of deriving it from the record's edges, so the marker goes stale and asserts a state that no longer holds.
records.formed_by: adding a status field that parties are trusted to keep current
detected_by: a status field whose value the record's edges contradict
measured_by: records carrying a written state

exemplar.before: status: absorbed is written and left in place → the record rests there as a marker
exemplar.after: absorbed is a transition → extract to the accumulator → delete in the same change

records.name: Invocation-Keyed Report
records.definition: A defect in which a run writes its result under a name derived from how it was invoked, beside the shared aggregate, so documents accumulate that each describe a moment and none the state.
records.formed_by: keying a report's filename on the scope, the caller or the flags of a run
detected_by: a report whose name carries a scope or caller segment
measured_by: keyed reports beside the aggregate

exemplar.before: report.<member>.json, report.<caller>.json → nobody prunes them → a reader cannot tell which is current
exemplar.after: one aggregate report → narrowed runs print their verdict

distinctFrom.reason: A narrowed aggregate overwrites the one aggregate with a partial result, while an invocation-keyed report writes a second document beside it.

records.name: Narrowed Aggregate
records.definition: A defect in which a run over a narrowed scope overwrites the whole-scope aggregate, so the aggregate reports a smaller population as though it were the whole.
records.formed_by: writing the aggregate from a run that measured part of its population
detected_by: an aggregate whose recorded population is smaller than the declared one
measured_by: aggregate writes from narrowed runs

exemplar.before: a run over one member writes the aggregate → the aggregate now reads clean for the whole tree
exemplar.after: the narrowed run streams its verdict → the aggregate keeps the last full run's result

records.name: Cyclic Tiebreak
records.definition: A defect in which a tiebreak picks a source among copies none of which is distinguished, turning a correct refusal into a direction no copy supports.
records.formed_by: breaking a tie by recency, path order or authorship when no copy derives from another and none is resolved
detected_by: a collapse direction chosen over a set with no distinguished copy
measured_by: collapses directed by a tiebreak

exemplar.before: no copy is the source → the newest file wins → every other copy is rewritten toward a value nobody decided
exemplar.after: no distinguished copy → refuse as a cycle → the decision stays with the party who holds the information

records.name: Destructive Closure
records.definition: A defect in which closing a converged venue deletes it instead of moving it to the archive, keeping the outcome and destroying the argument it came from.
records.formed_by: implementing a lifetime stated as deleted by removing the venue from the repository
detected_by: a closed venue that exists in neither the active surface nor the archive
measured_by: venues closed by deletion

exemplar.before: the venue converges → it is deleted → a later reader holds the ruling and cannot tell it from a preference
exemplar.after: the venue converges → its outcome is absorbed → the venue moves to the archive with every position intact

records.name: Hand-Kept Index
records.definition: A defect in which an index is written by hand beside what it indexes, so it drifts silently because nothing compares the two.
records.formed_by: adding and removing index entries by hand
detected_by: an index entry with no file, or a file with no entry
measured_by: entries and files missing their counterpart

exemplar.before: a seat file is added → the index is not edited → the scan resolves fewer seats than it reports
exemplar.after: the index is regenerated from the directory on every run
